The denominator is $4+7\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $4-7\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $4-7\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-6+5\text{i}}{4+7\text{i}} & =\frac{-6+5\text{i}}{4+7\text{i}}\cdot \frac{4-7\text{i}}{4-7\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{(-6+5\text{i})(4-7\text{i})}{(4+7\text{i})(4-7\text{i})} \\  & =\frac{-24+42\text{i}+20\text{i}-35{\text{i}}^{2}}{{4}^{2}-(7\text{i})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-24+62\text{i}-35(-1)}{{4}^{2}+{7}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-24+62\text{i}+35}{16+49} \\  & =\frac{11+62\text{i}}{65}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{11+62\text{i}}{65}=(\frac{11}{65})+(\frac{62}{65})\,\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$
